experiment: TUM fr1_room known-pose RGB SIFT local geometry
kept: real 640x480 TUM RGB (320x240 RGB for depth)
metric_scale: known metric poses + prior RGB-only anchor calibration; NOT monocular absolute scale
algorithm: OpenCV SIFT RGB features + RANSAC + calibrated triangulation + bounded regularized local depth deformation; no GPU; no new DA2 inference
visual_assessment: The source-camera desk and displays remain recognizable, but old and new images are nearly indistinguishable; free-view room structure is still severely warped and incomplete. Better sparse RGB anchor agreement and largest-component share are not room recovery.
limitations: Held-out sparse triangulated anchors are same-scene feature points, not independent surface truth. Five-view coverage is not geometric accuracy. Echo4D native browser rotation not tested. Original TUM is 640x480, not HD.
next: Use mature calibrated dense multi-view depth/geometry provider or RGB feature-track bundle geometry to address unsupported areas; preserve this failed control, stop tuning sparse local correction.
